items: The techniques of chromatography are very useful in organic synthesis for separation, isolation and purification of the products. They are equally important in qualitative and quantitative analyses and for determination of the purity of a substance.
Chromatography is very useful for identifying complicated chemicals such as dyes, drugs and pesticides.

blocks.prompt: a) On which basis the components of a mixture are separated from one another in paper chromatography?
blocks.explanation: Each component distributes itself differently between the stationary phase (water held in the cellulose of the paper) and the mobile phase (the organic solvent rising up the paper). A component that dissolves more in the mobile phase moves faster and further; one held more by the stationary phase stays behind. So each component has its own Rf value.

blocks.prompt: b) What are the stationary and mobile phases in paper chromatography?
blocks.explanation: Stationary phase: water held in the cellulose fibres of the paper. Mobile phase: the solvent that rises up the paper, usually an organic liquid that does not mix with this water.

blocks.prompt: c) How the purity of a substance is determined by using paper chromatography?
blocks.explanation: A chromatogram of the substance is run, alongside spots of known pure samples. A pure substance gives a single spot with the same Rf as the pure sample; more than one spot means that the substance is impure.
